name: Lip mask (overnight)

lead: An overnight lip mask is a heavy lip product worn during sleep so lips are softer and smoother by morning. It works like a thick lip balm.

Occlusive ingredients such as petrolatum and lanolin slow water loss from the lips, and thicker emollients give longer moisture retention. Medical-grade lanolin is noted by Wikipedia to speed healing of chapped lips. No studies of products marketed as lip masks were found.

paras: People apply a layer before bed and wipe or wash it off in the morning, often after a gentle exfoliation. It is part of a night-time skincare routine, with softer lips noticeable by the next morning.
Allergic reactions to ingredients such as beeswax and propolis have been reported. Anyone allergic to lanolin or a listed ingredient can check labels before use.

angle.text: Users leave a rich lip mask on during sleep to wake with softer, smoother lips. It sits in the same family as balm and petroleum jelly, whose barrier effect is documented. Appearance-specific trials are lacking.

lead: An overnight lip mask is a thick, occlusive lip treatment left on during sleep, in the same category as lip balm and petroleum jelly, which form a barrier that slows moisture loss from the lips [1][2]. Overnight balms are described as using thicker emollients such as lanolin for longer moisture retention. Wikipedia notes that medical-grade lanolin can speed healing of chapped lips [3].
No studies of products marketed as lip masks and no community sources were found.

paras: Petroleum jelly forms a barrier that slows moisture loss and can prevent chapped lips, and slugging, a related skincare practice, applies a thick layer before bed [2]. Contact allergy to lip-product ingredients such as beeswax and propolis has been reported.
